work: Pedeir Keinc y Mabinogi (the Four Branches of the Mabinogi)
edition: White Book of Rhydderch (NLW Peniarth 4, c. 1350), as printed diplomatically in J. Gwenogvryn Evans, The White Book Mabinogion (Pwllheli, 1907), cols 1–111 (Pwyll 1–38, Branwen 38–61, Manawydan 61–81, Math 81–111); scan: archive.org whitebookofmabin00evan, PDF pp. 33–88 (col c is on PDF page (c+65)//2, odd c = left column).
notes: opening/closing are in Evans's spelling and word division, with his sorts rendered per the conventions (6→w, r-rotunda→r, dotted y→y, long s→s; raised letters written raised). They are read off the page images.
words = word count of the matching stretch of the cy.wikisource witness (Williams-shaped word division, close to ours: the pilot's 2,198 established words against 2,204 there).

disagreements: OCR (letter-normalised) vs witness, counted cmp.py-style as non-equal alignment runs inside the part; 'glyph' = known misreadings of Evans's sorts (f for long s, i/l, j for y, a/i/^ for r-rotunda, etc.), resolvable without the image; 'loss' = single letter missing/added in the OCR, glance at the image; 'check' = everything else, must be checked on the image. Worklists in drafts/<id>-diffs.txt.

parts.part: The rider at the mound of Arberth
parts.opening: Athreigylgueith yd oed yn arberth priflys idaw
parts.closing: tric yn iach achoffa gywiraw dy edewit aᶜ eymdeith yd af i.
issues: Col 16, line 12 (PDF p. 40): Evans prints a blank space in the line 'Arglwyd heb [space] allu' – a White Book defect. Red Book (Rhŷs & Evans 1905): 'arglwyd heb ef nyt oes allu'. The sense requires 'nyt oes' (and the speech tag 'ef'): supply from the Red Book and say so in the note, per the conventions — decision on how much to supply (see LOG.md).

Col 14 line 1 (PDF p. 39, image checked): Evans prints 'na thygyei idaw idaw / y hymlit' – a scribal dittography of idaw (the witness has one). Decision: keep as written with a note (conventions: readable slips stay), or print once.
parts.name: The rider at the mound of Arberth
